docs.title: What is GSEA?
docs.text: Gene Set Enrichment Analysis asks a question that a list of individual genes can't answer on its own: is a whole set of related genes behaving differently between two conditions, even when no single gene screams for attention?

docs.title: The problem it solves
docs.text: Differential expression hands you a ranked list of genes. But biology rarely acts one gene at a time — pathways move together, often in small coordinated nudges. Twenty genes each shifting a little can matter more than one gene shifting a lot, and a gene-by-gene threshold will miss it entirely.

docs.title: The idea
docs.text: GSEA walks down your ranked list of all genes and asks whether the members of a given gene set cluster toward the top (or bottom) more than chance would predict. It accumulates a running enrichment score, then tests that score against permutations.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
import gsea

results = gsea.run(
    ranked_list=ranked_genes,   # (1)
    gene_sets=hallmark_sets,
    permutations=1000,
)

results.top(10)
  1. Genes ranked by your differential-expression statistic, most up-regulated first.

The output is a set of pathways with enrichment scores and adjusted p-values — the coordinated signals your per-gene analysis stepped right over.
